record.title: Belbachir et al.'s ray-unimodality conjecture for Pascal's triangle
record.statement: Let $\binom{n}{k}$ be a fixed element of Pascal's triangle, and let a ray cross a sequence of entries in the triangle. **Ray-unimodality conjecture.** The sequence of binomial coefficients located along this ray is unimodal. This conjecture extends known unimodality results for several families of binomial coefficient sequences, but its resolution is not indicated here.
record.source_name: Xun-Tuan Su and Yi Wang, “On unimodality problems in Pascal's triangle”, arXiv:0809.1579 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.1579

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

record.title: Haggard–Pearce–Royle conjecture on flow roots above five
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph, and let $\Phi_G(Q)$ denote its flow polynomial. **Haggard–Pearce–Royle conjecture.** For any bridgeless graph $G$, 
$$
\Phi_G(Q)>0\qquad\text{for }Q\in[5,\infty).
$$
 This is a proposed weakening of Welsh's conjecture after the explicit counterexample to the interval $(4,\infty)$; it retains the endpoint $Q=5$ in accordance with Tutte's five-flow conjecture.
record.source_name: Jesper L. Jacobsen and Jesus Salas, “Is the five-flow conjecture almost false?”, arXiv:1009.4062 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.4062

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2010).

record.title: The one-generation conjecture for the block algebra
record.statement: Let $\SB$ be an exceptional block, and let $A_\SB$ be the associated $A_\infty$ algebra. **One-generation conjecture.** The algebra $A_\SB$ is one-generated as an $A_\infty$ algebra, and its Koszul dual is an ordinary algebra. The conjecture is motivated by the explicit example in the paper; the general assertion is left open.
record.source_name: Alexander Kuznetsov and Alexander Polishchuk, “Exceptional collections on isotropic Grassmannians”, arXiv:1110.5607 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.5607

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: One-descent conjecture for generalized monotone triangles
record.statement:
Let $A_n:=\alpha(n;1,2,\ldots,n)$, and let $n\geq2$ and $i=1,\ldots,n-1$. **One-descent conjecture.** The identity

$$
A_n=\alpha(n+2;1,2,\ldots,i+1,i,i+1,\ldots,n)
$$

should hold. This is a computational conjecture related to a broader reverse-duplication identity developed later in the paper; the source does not provide a general proof.
record.source_name: Lukas Riegler, “Generalized Monotone Triangles: an extended Combinatorial Reciprocity Theorem”, arXiv:1207.4437 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2012).

record.title: A formula for a repeated-entry generalized monotone-triangle enumeration
record.statement:
Let $A_{n-1}:=\alpha(n-1;1,2,\ldots,n-1)$ and let $n\geq4$. **Repeated-entry formula conjecture.** The identity

$$
\alpha(n+1;1,3,4,3,4,5,\ldots,n)=\frac{n+4}{2}A_{n-1}
$$

should hold. The formula was obtained from computational experiments and is presented as part of a family of conjectured evaluations; no proof is given in the source.
record.source_name: Lukas Riegler, “Generalized Monotone Triangles: an extended Combinatorial Reciprocity Theorem”, arXiv:1207.4437 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.4437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2012).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for a fourth-power Wolstenholme congruence
record.statement:
Let $S_m(n)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^m$. **Fourth-power Wolstenholme congruence conjecture.** For no integer $n\ge 2$ does the congruence

$$
S_{n-2}(n)\equiv 0\pmod{n^4}
$$

hold. The source presents this as a computationally motivated strengthening of the Wolstenholme-prime criterion; no proof or counterexample is supplied.
record.source_name: Romeo Meštrović, “A congruence modulo n^3 involving two consecutive sums of powers and its applications”, arXiv:1211.4570 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4570

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2012). “Therefore, any counterexample to Giuga's conjecture must be squarefree.”

record.title: Cayley graph Hamilton-cycle conjecture
record.statement: Let $H$ be a finite group and let $S\subseteq H$ satisfy $S=S^{-1}$ and exclude the identity. The Cayley graph $G(H;S)$ has vertex set $H$, with $g,h\in H$ adjacent when $g=sh$ for some $s\in S$. **Cayley graph Hamilton-cycle conjecture.** Every connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices contains a Hamilton cycle. The conjecture is known when $H$ is abelian, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Hamilton cycles in graphs and hypergraphs: an extremal perspective”, arXiv:1402.4268 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4268

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: Hirsch's diameter conjecture for polyhedra
record.statement: Let $f > d \geq 2$. Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polyhedron with $f$ facets. **Hirsch's conjecture.** The combinatorial diameter of $P$ is at most $f-d$. The conjecture is false in general: Klee and Walkup found an unbounded counterexample in dimension $4$, and Santos later produced a bounded counterexample. It nevertheless holds for many important classes of polyhedra.
record.source_name: Tamon Stephen and Timothy Yusun, “Circuit diameter and Klee-Walkup constructions”, arXiv:1503.05252 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.05252

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2015). “This provides some evidence for Conjecture by establishing it in one place where Hirsch does not hold for the graph diameter.”

record.title: Blocki–Zwonek's convexity conjecture for Green-function sublevel sets
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^n$, let $w\in\Omega$, let $G_{\Omega,w}$ denote the pluricomplex Green's function of $\Omega$ with pole at $w$, and let $\lambda$ denote Lebesgue measure. **Blocki–Zwonek's conjecture.** The function

$$
t\longmapsto \log \lambda(\{G_{\Omega,w}<t\})
$$

should be convex. The paper gives a counterexample, so the conjecture is false.
record.source_name: John Erik Fornæss, “On a conjecture by Blocki-Zwonek”, arXiv:1507.05003 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05003

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Identity conjecture for words with countably many profinite values
record.statement: Let $w$ be a group-word and $G$ a profinite group. Suppose that the set of $w$-values in $G$ is countable. **Identity conjecture.** Then $G$ satisfies a nontrivial group identity. The paper presents this as a potentially more tractable conjecture than the preceding finiteness conjecture, and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Cristina Acciarri and Pavel Shumyatsky, “Coverings of commutators in profinite groups”, arXiv:1511.07843 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07843

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: The Valdivia compacta ccc dichotomy conjecture
record.statement: Let $K$ be a nonempty Valdivia compact space satisfying the countable chain condition (ccc). **Valdivia compacta ccc dichotomy conjecture.** Either $K$ has a $G_\delta$ point or $K$ admits a nontrivial convergent sequence in the complement of a dense $\Sigma$-subset. The paper presents a counterexample to this conjecture under $\diamondsuit$, so the asserted dichotomy is not valid in general.
record.source_name: Claudia Correa and Daniel V. Tausk, “Small Valdivia compacta and trees”, arXiv:1512.02610 (2016).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1505.06727](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06727).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.02610

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The non-occurrence of $zeta(2)$ as a $phi^4$ period
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_{\phi^4}$ denote the space of $\phi^4$ periods and let $\zeta(2)$ be the Riemann zeta value at $2$. **Non-occurrence conjecture.**

$$
\zeta(2)\notin\mathcal{P}_{\phi^4}.
$$

No $\phi^4$ graph is known to evaluate to $\zeta(2)$; the stronger expectation involving logarithmic and generalized Feynman periods is stated separately in the source.
record.source_name: Erik Panzer and Oliver Schnetz, “The Galois coaction on ϕ^4 periods”, arXiv:1603.04289 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04289

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

record.title: The strong Neuwirth conjecture for prime knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a prime knot other than a torus knot. An **essential non-orientable spanning surface** is a non-orientable spanning surface for $K$ that is essential in its exterior.

**Strong Neuwirth conjecture.** There exists an essential non-orientable spanning surface for $K$.

The source explicitly notes that Dunfield found a counterexample to this conjecture, so the claim is refuted.
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1103.2576](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.2576).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09039

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2016). “By a deep consideration on the graph which is obtained from the intersection between two planar surfaces which are obtained by restricting them on the knot exteriors, a contradiction can be reached.”

record.title: Strong Bordeaux Conjecture on 3-coloring planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph. **Strong Bordeaux Conjecture.** If no pair of cycles of length three in $G$ shares an edge and $G$ has no cycle of length five, then $G$ is 3-colorable. This conjecture is explicitly stated to be disproved by the same counterexample that disproves Steinberg's conjecture.
record.source_name: Vincent Cohen-Addad, Michael Hebdige, Daniel Kral, Zhentao Li and Esteban Salgado, “Steinberg's Conjecture is false”, arXiv:1604.05108 (2016).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1508.07890](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.07890), [arXiv:1004.0582](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0582).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.05108

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2016); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The torsion-freeness conjecture for lbo homology
record.statement: Let $X$ be a shelf, and let $H_*^{\mathrm{lbo}}(X)$ denote its lbo homology groups. **Torsion-freeness conjecture.** There is no torsion in $H_*^{\mathrm{lbo}}(X)$. The conjecture is suggested by the limited computational data discussed for lbo homology; no proof or counterexample is given in the source.
record.source_name: Sujoy Mukherjee, “A Homology Theory For A Special Family Of Semi-groups”, arXiv:1611.05555 (2016).

record.title: Polynomial Bézout identity for consecutive q-powers
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers. **Polynomial Bézout conjecture.** There exist polynomials $A_{n,r}$ and $B_{n,r}$ in $q$ with integer coefficients such that

$$
A_{n,r}(1-q^n)^r+B_{n,r}(1-q^{n+1})^r=(1-q)^r.
$$

This conjecture concerns an integral Bézout identity related to the preceding polynomial-coprimality argument; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo and Qiang-Qiang Jiang, “Factors of alternating sums of powers of q-Narayana numbers”, arXiv:1703.00003 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00003

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2017). “Numerical calculation implies that Conjecture does not hold when $j\geqslant 2r$.”

record.title: Limiting distribution of quadratic-character sums with a random phase
record.statement:
Let $chi_q$ be a quadratic character. What is the limiting distribution of
$$
S(\chi_q,x,\theta)=\sum_{n\le x}\chi_q(n)e(n\theta)
$$
when $theta\in[0,1]$ is chosen uniformly at random and $q\to\infty$?

record.title: Mahler problem for Littlewood polynomials
record.statement:
The report asks for the value of
\[
b_m=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{M_0(P_n)}{\sqrt n},
\]
where
\[
P_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_kx^k,\qquad a_k\in\{\pm1\}.
\]
The same report proves only the lower bound \(b_m>0.954\) by constructing Littlewood polynomials of arbitrarily large degree.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299577), page 13. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Even-order logarithmic Chowla conjecture
record.statement:
For every even integer $k\ge 4$ and any distinct integers $h_1,\ldots,h_k$, prove that
\[
\sum_{n\le X}\frac{1}{n}\lambda(n+h_1)\cdots\lambda(n+h_k)=o(\log X)\qquad (X\to\infty),
\]
where $\lambda(n)=(-1)^{\Omega(n)}$ is the Liouville function and $\Omega(n)$ counts prime factors with multiplicity.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299577), page 14. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: L¹ means of exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
record.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to[-1,1]$ be a multiplicative function such that
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\le N}f(n)^2>0.$$ If
$$\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le N}f(n)e(n\alpha)\right|\,d\alpha<N^{o(1)}\qquad(N\to\infty),$$
then there exists a quadratic character $\chi$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, the set of primes $p$ satisfying $|f(p)-\chi(p)|\le\delta$ has logarithmic density equal to one.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299577), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Erdős’s integer dilation approximation problem under condition (3)
record.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ be a countable set such that
\[
\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{1}{\log x}\sum_{\alpha\in A\cap[1,x]}\frac{1}{\alpha}>0.
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a pair $(\alpha,\beta)\in A^2$ such that $\alpha\ne\beta$ and
\[
|n\alpha-\beta|<\varepsilon
\]
for some positive integer $n$.

record.title: The 1/3–2/3 Conjecture for finite non-chain posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset that is not a chain. For distinct $x,y\in P$, let
$$
\delta_{xy}=\min\{\mathbb{P}(x\prec y),\mathbb{P}(y\prec x)\},
$$
where the probability is taken over a uniformly random linear extension of $P$, and set
$$
\delta(P)=\max_{x\ne y}\delta_{xy}.
$$
The conjecture asserts that
$$
\delta(P)\ge \frac{1}{3}.
$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 32. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Polylogarithmic treewidth for induced-minor-free graph classes
record.statement:
For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an integer $d=d(t)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{C}_t^*$ with $n>2$ satisfies
$$
\operatorname{tw}(G)\le \log^d n.
$$
Here $\mathcal{C}_t$ is the class of graphs with no induced minor isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ or the $t\times t$ hexagonal grid $W_{t\times t}$, and $\mathcal{C}_t^*$ is the subclass containing no complete subgraph of size $t$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 37. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Every bounded operator on an infinite-dimensional Banach space has norm attainment
record.statement: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ such that every bounded linear operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,X)$ attains its norm; that is, for every $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,X)$ there exists $x\in X$ with $\lVert x\rVert=1$ and $\lVert Tx\rVert=\lVert T\rVert$?

record.title: Green problem 32
record.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ be a set of size $\lfloor \sqrt{p} \rfloor$. Is there a dilate of $A$ containing a gap of length $100\sqrt{p}$?

record.title: Green problem 44
record.statement: Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes $2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most $\frac{1}{10} N$? We interpret "half the residue classes" as $\lfloor p_i / 2 \rfloor$.

record.title: Green problem 58
record.statement: Suppose $A, B ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ both have size at least $N^{0.49}$. Must the sumset $A + B$ contain a composite number?

record.title: Green problem 66
record.statement: Is there always a sum of two squares between $X - \frac{1}{10}X^{1/4}$ and $X$? We formalize this as an eventual statement for sufficiently large real $X$.

record.title: Green problem 72
record.statement: **Green's Open Problem 72 / No-three-in-line problem**: For $N$ sufficiently large, is it impossible to have $2N$ points in $[N]^2$ with no three in a line? Green suspects the answer is yes, and that $(3/2 + o(1))N$ is optimal.

record.title: OEIS A179524 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A179524](https://oeis.org/A179524), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

If $p$ is a prime with $p \equiv 1, 9 \pmod{20}$ and $p = x^2 + 5y^2$ with $x, y$ integers, then $\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} a(k) \equiv 4x^2 - 2p \pmod{p^2}$. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Jul 01 2010

record.title: OEIS A179537 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A179537](https://oeis.org/A179537), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

If $p$ is a prime with $(p/7) = 1$ and $p = x^2 + 7y^2$ with $x, y$ integers, then $\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} (-1)^k a(k) \equiv 4x^2 - 2p \pmod{p^2}$. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Jul 17 2010

record.title: OEIS A180017 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A180017](https://oeis.org/A180017), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

"This sequence is positive on average, since 1/log(3) > 1/log(4). Do all integers appear infinitely often?" - Charles R Greathouse IV, Feb 07 2013

record.title: OEIS A182126 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A182126](https://oeis.org/A182126), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

Conjecture: For $x > 10^9$, the most frequent value in $a(n)$, $n=1\dots x$, has form $120k$.

record.title: OEIS A000224 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A000224](https://oeis.org/A224), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

$n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{a(n)(a(n)-1)}$ if and only if $n$ is an odd prime. - Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017

record.title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture for prime-counting errors
record.statement: The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture: for every $\theta < 1$ and $A > 0$ there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that $$\sum_{1 \le q \le x^{\theta}} E(x; q) \le \frac{C x}{\log^A x}$$ for all $x > 2$.

record.title: Completeness of Euler’s idoneal numbers
record.statement:
Is Euler’s list of 65 idoneal numbers complete? The exact list and idoneal-number predicate are defined in the linked Lean statement.

Idoneal numbers completeness conjecture.

record.title: Payne’s inequality conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain, or more generally a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, and let $\lambda_k$ denote the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplace--Beltrami operator and $\Lambda_k$ the $k$-th buckling eigenvalue. Payne's conjecture asserts that $\lambda_k\leq\Lambda_k$ for every $k\geq 1$.
record.references: - [A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20097) — arXiv — Davide Buoso, Vladimir Lotoreichik
